name: dependably
description: Ask Claude about the packages, vulnerabilities and licences in your Dependably registry.
long_description:
Dependably is a private artefact repository and pull-through proxy for npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, RPM, OCI, Go, Cargo, apk, Terraform and Hex, self-hosted or run as a hosted SaaS instance. This extension connects Claude to your own instance with a personal access token you create there.

With it, Claude can list and search your packages, look up a package before you adopt it, and explain an advisory and its fix. It can also scope your vulnerability report to one project's lockfile with the version to bump to, check a licence against your policy, and write the install or publish command for the eight ecosystems that have one. Two more tools check whether the registry itself is up and healthy. Every tool is read-only: none of them can change or delete anything in your registry.

All traffic goes straight from your machine to your own Dependably instance, and nowhere else. Your token stays in your operating system's keychain. Instances behind a private certificate authority are supported through an optional CA bundle setting; there is no option to disable certificate verification.

Requires Dependably v0.3.0 or later and a token with `read:packages` — the Pull preset, which any member can create.

tools.name: check_dependencies
tools.description: Scope the org-wide vulnerability report to ONE project's dependency list and return only what affects it, each package annotated with the version to bump to. Prefer this over list_vulnerabilities whenever the question is about a specific project or lockfile — read the lockfile yourself and pass the resolved dependencies as `packages`. For an npm package-lock.json (v2/v3) that is every entry of its `packages` map: `{ name, version, dev }`. Also answers "is this clean now?" after a fix: `clean` is true when nothing matched. Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: get_install_command
tools.description: Return the shell command to install a package through this Dependably instance. This tool DOES NOT execute — show the command to the user and let them run it.

tools.name: get_license_policy
tools.description: The org's license policy: enforcement mode (off/warn/block) plus the SPDX allowlist and blocklist (GET /api/v1/license-policy) — answers "which licenses are approved here". Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: get_package
tools.description: Full detail for one package: versions, per-version SPDX licenses, vulnerability links (GET /api/v1/packages/{ecosystem}/{name}). Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: get_publish_command
tools.description: Return the shell command to publish an artifact through this Dependably instance. This tool DOES NOT execute — show the command to the user and let them run it. Replace <token> with a valid Dependably token.

tools.name: get_remediation
tools.description: Fixed version (plus CWE / OWASP / remediation-skill ids) for one or more advisories, without the full advisory prose. Pass the installed version alongside each id to get the fix for that release line — for @hono/node-server 1.19.14 that is 1.19.15, not the 2.x fix. Use get_vulnerability instead when you need the write-up, PoC, or workarounds. Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: get_remediation_skill
tools.description: Full how-to-fix guide for one or more curated remediation skills, as markdown (GET /api/v1/remediation/skills/{skillId}). Skill ids come from list_remediation_skills, or from the `skills` field get_remediation and check_dependencies return with includeAdvisoryDetail. Anonymous — no capability required.

tools.name: get_vulnerability
tools.description: Rich detail for one advisory affecting the registry (GET /api/v1/vulnerabilities/{osvId}). 404 if the advisory does not touch any package in your org. Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: Liveness probe (GET /health). Returns 200 with { status: "ok" } as long as the process is running.

tools.name: list_packages
tools.description: List packages in the registry, paginated (GET /api/v1/packages). Returns { items, total, limit, offset }. Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: list_remediation_skills
tools.description: Index of every curated remediation skill this instance ships (GET /api/v1/remediation/skills): id, name and description, one per vulnerability class (vulnerable dependency, injection, XSS, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, SSRF, broken access control, weak cryptography, authentication failures). Pass an id to get_remediation_skill for the full how-to-fix guide. Anonymous — no capability required.

tools.name: list_vulnerabilities
tools.description: Org-wide vulnerability report: every package in the registry affected by a known advisory, paginated (GET /api/v1/vuln-report). Returns { items, total, limit, offset }. This is the whole org, NOT one project — to scope it to a project's dependencies and get bump targets, use check_dependencies. Items are compact by default; pass verbosity "full" for the raw server fields. Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: lookup_package
tools.description: Pre-adoption check of a package NOT necessarily in the registry: upstream metadata, OSV advisories, and the org-policy verdict, without ingesting anything (GET /api/v1/lookup). Use before adding a new dependency. Requires read:packages capability.

tools.name: readiness_check
tools.description: Readiness probe (GET /ready). Returns { status: "ready"|"degraded", checks, errors }. 503 with details when a subsystem (DB, blob store, etc.) is failing — use this first when investigating an incident.

tools.name: search_packages
tools.description: Quick search across the registry by name (GET /api/v1/search). Queries shorter than 2 characters return empty groups. Requires read:packages capability.

base_url.title: Dependably URL
base_url.description: The address of your Dependably instance, for example https://registry.example.com. On a multi-tenant host, use your organization's subdomain.

token.title: Personal access token
token.description: Create one in Dependably under Tokens. The Pull preset is enough — every tool this extension offers works on it.

timeout_ms.title: Request timeout (milliseconds)
timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for a single request to your instance.

ca_bundle.title: Private CA bundle (optional)
ca_bundle.description: Only if your Dependably instance uses a certificate from a private CA: a PEM file containing the CA certificate chain. Leave empty for public certificates.
